name: Tocilizumab
route_note: IV infusion every 4 weeks or subcutaneous injection weekly or every other week
originator: Chugai Pharmaceutical and Osaka University (Tadamitsu Kishimoto)
owner: Roche (Chugai in Japan); biosimilars from several companies

discovery.note: Humanised IgG1 antibody against the IL-6 receptor, building on Kishimoto's discovery of IL-6 in 1986.

tagline: IL-6 receptor blocker for arthritis, giant cell arteritis, CAR T toxicity and COVID-19
summary: Tocilizumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody that blocks both soluble and membrane-bound interleukin-6 receptors. It is used in rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, giant cell arteritis, cytokine release syndrome after CAR T-cell therapy and hospitalised COVID-19.
mechanism: IL-6 signals through IL-6R and the gp130 co-receptor, either on cells expressing membrane IL-6R (classic signalling) or via soluble IL-6R (trans-signalling), driving JAK–STAT3 activation, acute-phase protein production, B- and T-cell responses and fever.
Tocilizumab binds both forms of IL-6R and prevents IL-6 binding. CRP falls rapidly, so it can mask the usual signs of infection.
uses: Polyarticular and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis
CAR T cell-induced cytokine release syndrome
Hospitalised COVID-19 on corticosteroids and oxygen

history.title: IL-6 cloned
history.detail: Kishimoto and Hirano at Osaka University clone the gene for IL-6.

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Approved in Japan for multicentric Castleman disease.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the EU as RoActemra for rheumatoid arthritis.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in January for rheumatoid arthritis.

history.title: GCA and CRS
history.detail: Approved for giant cell arteritis (GiACTA) and for CAR T-cell cytokine release syndrome.

history.title: COVID-19
history.detail: RECOVERY shows reduced mortality in hospitalised patients; FDA grants emergency use authorisation in June.

history.title: Full COVID-19 approval
history.detail: FDA approves tocilizumab for hospitalised COVID-19 in December.

history.title: First biosimilar
history.detail: FDA approves Tofidence (tocilizumab-bavi); Tyenne follows in 2024.

pk.half_life: Concentration-dependent; up to ~11–13 days at steady state
pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

safety.boxed_warning: Serious infections, including tuberculosis, bacterial, invasive fungal, viral and other opportunistic infections.

facts: It was the first IL-6 pathway inhibitor approved.
Because it suppresses CRP and fever, infections may present with few signs during treatment.
